sentences.text:
Crr No. 5108 of 2023
 (Mangilal Savita Vs The State Of Madhya
 Dated : 16-10-2024
Mr. Ram Kishor Sharma - Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Saket Naresh Udainiya - P.P. for respondent/State.
Heard on I.A. No. 20198 of 2023, an application for exemption from surrendering before the trial Court.
Application is duly supported by an affidavit along with the relevant documents in relation to continuous treatment of heart ailment since 2019 of the present petitioner.

Counsel for the petitioner submitted that petitioner is suffering from heart ailment for long period of time, under these circumstances, he may be exempted from surrender before the learned trial Court.
In view of facts and circumstances of the case and having considered the documents, application is allowed.
Also heard on the question of admission.
This criminal revision appears to be arguable, hence, it is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No. 20082/2023, which is First application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the petitioner.

This criminal revision under Section 397 read with Section 401 of CR.P.C. is preferred by the petitioner challenging the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 12.10.2023 passed by Third Additional Sessions Judge, Jaura, District Morena (M.P.) affirming the judgment of conviction and sentence dated 24.04.2017 passed in Criminal Case No.148/2011 by Judicial Magistrate, First 2 CRR-5108-2023 Class, Jaura, Dist. Morena (M.P.) whereby, petitioner has been Mangilal Savita vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5417963/
1 convicted and sentenced under Section16(1)(A)(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act to undergo maximum six months RI with maximum fine of Rs. 1000/- with default stipulation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the Courts below have wrongly appreciated the evidence and convicted the petitioner.
It is further submitted that there are material contradictions and omissions in the statement of prosecution witnesses.
Present revision is likely to take long time to come up for final hearing.
Hence, prayed to suspend the jail sentence of the petitioner looking to the short period of jail sentence and release him on bail.
On the other hand, learned State counsel opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the application (I.A.No. 20082/2023) is allowed.

It is directed that the petitioner be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court.
The petitioner shall now appear before the Registry of this Court on 18.12.2024 and on all other dates which may be given by the Office for his appearance till final disposal of the present case.
Certified copy/e-copy as per rules/directions.
(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE (LJ*) 3 CRR-5108-2023
